title: The Wood of the Cross
english: Look, beloved, at Rome, the imperial city, glorying in the emblems of the cross in the middle of her marketplace. Look at Paul, writing his undying letters and recording himself as a servant of the cross. He was not ashamed of the cross, the stumbling block of the Jews; what the Gentiles call foolishness he took up as a safeguard of wisdom (1 Corinthians 1:23). By the wood of the cross he roused the churches throughout the world.

A single rod of Moses drove off the plagues of the Egyptians, but a rod akin to the wood of the cross puts an end to the sins of humankind. There Pharaoh is drowned in the sea while pursuing Israel (Exodus 14:23–28); here the devil is overthrown, and those who worship the Savior are saved. There Adam stretched out his hands and drew death upon us (Genesis 3:6); but our Master, by stretching out his hands, saved all things.

But O wood, more magnificent than heaven and higher than the vaults of the sky! O thrice-blessed wood, ferrying our souls across to heaven! O wood that won salvation for the world and drove out the devil's army! O wood that hurled the thief into paradise like a javelin and set him dancing with Christ: 'For truly, truly I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise' (Luke 23:43).
Let us imitate the good resolve of the murderer, or rather of the bearer of the Spirit…
translator_notes: The row opens mid-sentence: u01-open ends 'then across the world's…' (τότε τῷ τῆς οἰκουμένης), and κύκλῳ κατέλαμψεν ('…whole circle he shone out') completes it, with the Word (the lamp set on the lampstand) as subject. κύκλῳ, 'the round, the circle', is rendered 'whole circle' to carry its sense of the entire round of the world. The English opens with a leading ellipsis.

τὴν βασιλεύουσαν Ῥώμην: 'the reigning (city)', the standard title for the imperial capital; rendered 'the imperial city'. σεμνυνομένην: 'made stately / taking pride in'; rendered 'glorying in'. The reference is to crosses set up in public places in Rome.

δοῦλον τοῦ σταυροῦ ἑαυτὸν καταγράψαντα: 'recording himself as a servant of the cross'. Paul calls himself δοῦλος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ (Romans 1:1), never 'servant of the cross' in those words; οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη may recall Romans 1:16 (οὐ γὰρ ἐπαισχύνομαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον) and Galatians 6:14 (boasting in the cross). These are possible allusions only and are not cited inline.

τὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν μωρίαν σοφίας ἐπεσπάσατο φυλακτήριον: object 'the foolishness of the Gentiles', predicate 'safeguard (amulet) of wisdom'; rendered 'what the Gentiles call foolishness he took up as a safeguard of wisdom'. 'call' makes explicit that the foolishness is the Gentiles' verdict on the cross, as in 1 Corinthians 1:23.

Μία ῥάβδος μωσαϊκὴ τὰς τῶν Αἰγυπτίων μάστιγας ἀπήλασεν: ἀπελαύνω is 'drive away / drive off'. In Exodus the rod brings the plagues on and also ends several (for example Exodus 9:33; 10:13, 19); the source wording is kept as 'drove off' and no inline citation is given because no single verse is in view. ἐπήλασεν ('drove upon') would be an easy correction, but the copy-text has ἀπήλασεν and it is not emended.
ῥάβδος δὲ συγγενείᾳ πρὸς τὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ ξύλον: 'a rod by kinship to the wood of the cross'; rendered 'a rod akin to the wood of the cross'. The present tense παύει ('puts an end to') is kept.
ἐνταῦθα δὲ διάβολος καταλύεται: 'here', at the cross; καταλύω rendered 'overthrown'.
ὁ ἡμέτερος δεσπότης: 'our Master'. The contrast is Adam's outstretched hands at the tree and Christ's outstretched hands on the cross.

διαπορθμεῦον: 'ferrying across', the image of a ferry crossing to heaven. λῃστὴν εἰς παράδεισον ἀκοντίσαν: ἀκοντίζω is 'hurl a javelin'; rendered 'hurled the thief into paradise like a javelin'. μετὰ Χριστοῦ χορεύειν πεποιηκός: 'made him dance with Christ'; rendered 'set him dancing with Christ'.

The row closes mid-sentence: τοῦ πνευματοφόρου continues with διὰ τὴν μετὰ ταῦτα πίστιν in u01-rem-mid. ἀνδροφόνος is 'man-slayer, murderer'; πνευματοφόρος 'bearer of the Spirit', capitalised because the Holy Spirit is meant. The English closes with an ellipsis.
Soft and line-break splits in the source (κατέ λαμψεν, συμ-βόλοις, ἀθα νάτους, ἑαυ τὸν, σκάν δαλον, μω ρίαν, συγ γενείᾳ, ἁ μαρτήματα, ἐκτεί νας, οὐρα νίους) are joined; no letters were added.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia i in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 rem early

title: Remember Me in Your Kingdom
english: …because of the faith that came afterward. For what does he say? 'Remember me, Lord, in your kingdom' (Luke 23:42). And by a single assent of faith he dwells in paradise and walks about the heavens. 'For truly I say to you,' he says, 'today you will be with me in paradise' (Luke 23:43).
Let us too remain beside the Savior's cross, saying these very words: 'Lord, remember me in your kingdom' (Luke 23:42), so that we too may become sharers in paradise and enjoy the kingdom of heaven.

The present festival, brothers, is a feast of victory, the victory feast of the Son of God, the King of all. For today the devil has been defeated through the one who was crucified, and our race rejoices because of the one who rose.

For this day cries out to me as I rise, and says: "In my course I saw a new sight: a tomb being opened, and a man being raised, and bones exulting, and souls rejoicing, and human beings being fashioned, and the heavens being torn open, and the powers crying out, 'Lift up your gates, you rulers' (Psalm 24:7), and the rest. Today I saw the heavenly King ascending, girded with light, above lightning and sunbeams, above the sun and the springs of waters, above the clouds, and with a spirit of power and eternal life."
translator_notes: The row opens mid-sentence: διὰ τὴν μετὰ ταῦτα πίστιν completes 'of the bearer of the Spirit' at the end of u01-rem-early; the thief is so called 'because of the faith that came afterward'. The English opens with an ellipsis.
ἐν μιᾷ συγκαταθέσει πίστεως: 'by a single assent of faith'. οἰκεῖ and περιπολεῖ are present tense ('dwells', 'walks about') and are kept.
Νικητήριον: a feast or prize of victory; rendered 'feast of victory' and 'victory feast'. τοῦ παμβασιλέως υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ: 'the Son of God, the King of all'.

διὰ τὸν σταυρωθέντα / διὰ τὸν ἀναστάντα: διά with the accusative is 'because of / on account of'; the first is rendered 'through the one who was crucified' because the devil's defeat is the Crucified One's act, the second 'because of the one who rose'.

Βοᾷ γὰρ ἡ σήμερον ἡμέρα τῇ ἐγέρσει μου: the dative τῇ ἐγέρσει μου ('to / at my rising, awakening') is hard. It is taken as the preacher's rising (from sleep for the vigil, or to speak): 'this day cries out to me as I rise'. It could also be read as part of the day's own voice ('at my dawning'). The day's speech that follows is set in double quotation marks; it closes after ζωὴν αἰώνιον, and Οὗτος γὰρ is the preacher again.
Ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ δρόμῳ: 'in my course', the day's course from dawn to dusk.

ὀστέα ἀγαλλιώμενα may echo LXX Psalm 50:10 (Psalm 51:8, ἀγαλλιάσονται ὀστέα τεταπεινωμένα); οὐρανοὺς σχιζομένους matches the wording of Mark 1:10 (σχιζομένους τοὺς οὐρανούς) but there it is the Baptism; ἀνθρώπους πλασσομένους may recall the forming of man in Genesis 2:7 (ἔπλασεν). All three are possible allusions only and are not cited inline. πλασσομένους is rendered 'being fashioned' without adding 'anew'.

περιεζωσμένον φῶς, ὑπὲρ ἀστραπὴν καὶ ἀκτῖνας, ὑπὲρ ἥλιον καὶ πηγὰς ὑδάτων, ὑπὲρ νεφέλας καὶ πνεῦμα δυνάμεως καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον: the three ὑπέρ phrases are taken with the ascent ('ascending … above'), and πνεῦμα δυνάμεως καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον as further objects of περιεζωσμένον ('girded … with a spirit of power and eternal life'), since 'above eternal life' would make no sense. The English keeps the Greek order and marks the change with 'and with'. 'Spirit' here is lower case: 'a spirit of power' describes what the King is clothed with, not the person of the Holy Spirit; the reading is uncertain. Psalm 92:1 LXX (ἐνεδύσατο κύριος δύναμιν καὶ περιεζώσατο) is a possible echo, not cited inline.
ἀκτῖνας rendered 'sunbeams' (rays of the sun), which the following ἥλιον supports.
The row closes mid-sentence: Οὗτος γὰρ ἐκρύβη πρῶτον continues with μὲν ἐν κοιλίᾳ σαρκός in u01-rem-close. The English closes with an ellipsis.
The page number '1' between lines in the source block is an editorial page marker and is omitted.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia i in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 rem mid

title: The Lord Risen and Enthroned
english: …in a womb of flesh, and then in the womb of the earth: in the one, sanctifying those who are born, through his being carried in the womb; in the other, giving life to the dead, through his resurrection. 'For pain and sorrow and sighing have fled away' (Isaiah 35:10). 'For who has known the mind of God, or who has been his counselor?' (Romans 11:34; Isaiah 40:13) Who, except the Word, who became flesh, was nailed to the wood, rose from the dead, and was lifted up into the heavens?
This day is the good news of joy. For on this day the Lord rose, and raised with him the flock of Adam. For he was born for the sake of man, and he rose in man.

Today, through the one who rose, paradise has been opened, Adam is given life, Eve is comforted, the calling is multiplied, the kingdom is made ready, man is saved, and Christ is worshipped. For he trampled down death, took the tyrant captive, and plundered Hades, and then he went up into the heavens as a victorious king, as a glorious commander, as a charioteer never overtaken, saying to the Father, 'Here am I, and the children whom you have given me, O God' (Hebrews 2:13; Isaiah 8:18), and the rest. And he heard from the Father, 'Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet' (Psalm 110:1).
To him be the glory, now and to the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: The row opens mid-sentence: μὲν ἐν κοιλίᾳ σαρκός completes Οὗτος γὰρ ἐκρύβη πρῶτον at the end of u01-rem-mid ('For he was hidden, first…'). The English opens with an ellipsis.
ἐν κοιλίᾳ τῆς γῆς: 'in the womb of the earth', the tomb. It may recall Matthew 12:40 (ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ τῆς γῆς), but the noun differs, so it is not cited inline.

ὅπου μὲν … ὅπου δὲ: 'in the one … in the other'. ἁγιάζων τοὺς γεννωμένους διὰ τῆς κυήσεως: 'sanctifying those who are born through his being carried in the womb'; κύησις is pregnancy or gestation, and 'his' makes explicit that it is Christ's own gestation, as the parallel διὰ τῆς ἀναστάσεως (his resurrection) requires.

ἀλλ' ἢ ὁ Λόγος: 'except the Word'; the question expects the answer that only the incarnate Word knows the mind of God. The English sets the quotation as one question and Hesychius's reply as a second question, keeping his rhetorical form. σαρκωθείς ('became flesh, was incarnate') may recall John 1:14 but is creedal wording here and is not cited inline. Word is capitalised as a title of Christ.
Αὕτη ἡ ἡμέρα χαρᾶς εὐαγγελισμός: 'This day is the good news of joy'. It may echo Luke 2:10 (εὐαγγελίζομαι ὑμῖν χαρὰν μεγάλην); possible allusion only.

συνεγείρας τὴν τοῦ Ἀδὰμ ἀγέλην: 'raised with him the flock of Adam', that is, Adam's descendants. ἐγεννήθη γὰρ διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ ἀνέστη ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ: 'born for the sake of man, and he rose in man', in the human nature he took. 'man' here means humankind, as in the next sentence (ἄνθρωπος σῴζεται, 'man is saved').
κλῆσις πληθύνεται: 'the calling is multiplied', the number of the called grows. βασιλεία ἑτοιμάζεται may recall Matthew 25:34 (τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν); possible allusion only.

αἰχμαλωτίσας τὸν τύραννον … ἀνέβη εἰς οὐρανούς may recall LXX Psalm 67:19 (Psalm 68:18, ἀναβὰς εἰς ὕψος ᾐχμαλώτευσας αἰχμαλωσίαν) and Ephesians 4:8; the wording differs ('the tyrant', not 'captivity'), so it is not cited inline. The three aorist participles are rendered as main verbs in sequence ('he trampled … took … plundered, and then he went up') to keep the English natural; the order of events is the Greek's.

ἡνίοχος ἄλειπτος: ἄλειπτος would mean 'unanointed' (from ἀλείφω), which does not fit. It is read as ἄληπτος ('not to be caught, never overtaken'), a common itacistic spelling, giving 'a charioteer never overtaken'. Uncertain; the copy-text is not emended.
Doxology: Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα, νῦν καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν: 'To him be the glory, now and to the ages of ages. Amen.' Father is capitalised as a divine name throughout.
The trailing page number '2' at the end of the source block is an editorial page marker and is omitted. Line-break splits (βα σιλεὺς, λέ-γων) are joined; no letters were added.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia i in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 rem close
